So there is a written document who says something about your meeting, and Duncan himself also testified to the same effect.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, I can claim with full responsibility before this Trial Chamber that Colonel Alistair Duncan never informed me of some Croats having been kidnapped in Travnik. Similarly, Your Honours, I claim with full responsibility that I signed an order, or perhaps even two orders, on behalf of the 3rd Corps commander according to which the El mujahedin detachment was to be resubordinated to the Bosanska Krajina OG, which was led by the late General Alagic. So if I said that Colonel Alistair Duncan probably paraphrased what I said, but I would like to emphasise the fact that Colonel Alistair Duncan never told me that Croats had been kidnapped in Travnik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: Maybe I have not quite correctly presented the whole matter to you. I started by saying that some Croats had been kidnapped in Travnik in October and that one person was beheaded, according to the indictment. Then I went to the document, saying that Duncan had a conversation with you about difficulties with mujahedin in Travnik. Now, maybe this is not related to the kidnapping of the Croats but to some other difficulty in Travnik at the time, in October 1993. I don't know. But as far as we know, we only heard about one problem with the mujahedin in Travnik, and that concerns the kidnapping of a number of Croats. So this explains my reasoning. But if you are able to tell me that there were other difficulties that you have discussed with Duncan at the time, please tell me.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, I did talk to Colonel Alistair in very general terms, that members of the El mujahedin detachment or foreigners were a problem for the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. On several occasions before this Trial Chamber I have explained how we tried to deal with this problem, and our conversation has to be regarded in that context. And what I have testified about here has to be put in that context. That problem persisted all the while I was a member of the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: That is right. I agree with you totally there. But on the other hand, this is specific. It is "to resolve the ongoing problems with the mujahedin in Travnik in October 1993." The "ongoing problem." So it's not about mujahedin in general, but it's referring to something specific for Travnik in October 1993. Do you recall any conversations on that topic at that time?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, I claim with full responsibility that I never spoke about the problem of kidnapped Croats or the problem of mujahedin in October in Travnik with Colonel Alistair Duncan. And more specifically, I never discussed with him the case of kidnapped Croats in Travnik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: All right. Now, this was the reason why I put some -- I wanted to put some questions to you on the events in Travnik. The events themselves, were you aware of that at that time? Were you aware at the time in October 1993 that there was a problem with Croat civilians having been kidnapped?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. I wasn't aware of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: Did you ever become acquainted with the events? Was there any later moment in which you heard about them? And when was that?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, in the last month or so, this has been mentioned in the media in Bosnia-Herzegovina. You can hear about that on TV and on radio. I know that proceedings are being carried out in Bosnia-Herzegovina with regard to this case. And now I know the details because the media have been following the court proceedings very closely. However, if we are talking about October and the short period thereafter, I didn't know about the kidnapping of Croats in Travnik. I didn't know that a Croat had been beheaded. I didn't know it, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: Okay, thank you. Okay, thank you. That's what I wanted to ask you. Well, let's now discuss the -- what appears to be the main subject of your testimony, judging what has been said and asked the previous days over the previous two weeks. The foreign fighters subject, I would like to discuss with you. And I do this mainly on the basis of documents. And you have already seen a document given by the Defence to you at the beginning of your testimony on so-called mujahedins, and it would be helpful to have it again. If the Registrar could give you that binder. There are some other documents, too, that I may show to you. My main purpose is -- of this exercise is to -- not the only purpose, but maybe the main purpose is to have a good understanding of what the documents say. I would like to put you a number of things that come up with me if I read these documents. You said at the beginning of your testimony that you had a meeting with Halilovic, that Halilovic had a meeting with commanders of the 3rd Corps in April 1993. Later on, a document was shown to you, a war diary dated April 1993 which shows that indeed, in the evening of 21 April, starting at 2330, there was a meeting in which you participated, and you told us about it. I have a few questions to put to you with regard to this meeting and what happened before. The first thing that I would like to ask you is the following. Is it true, as some witness has said to us before, that on the same day - in the morning or the afternoon, I don't know - there was another meeting with the European monitors on a cease-fire that should or could be concluded between the army and the HVO. Was there a meeting, do you recall, on the possibility of concluding a cease-fire between the parties?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: And was it also the case that Halilovic was present at that meeting?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: And my third question with regard to that meeting is the following: Was that a meeting in which the international observers voiced criticism with regard to the presence of foreign fighters? I know that you said in your previous testimony several times "the international community criticised us." What I want to know is whether this criticism was also voiced in this meeting of the 21st of April on the cease-fire.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, I remember this meeting which involved representatives of the BiH Army, the HV, and the HVO. This meeting was held in Zenica under the auspices of the European monitors. I remember that the main topic of that meeting was cease-fire and putting an end to the fighting between the BiH Army and the HVO. This was the main focus of that meeting as far as I can remember. I cannot remember any discussion on mujahedin at that meeting. I do not exclude the possibility that mujahedin may have been discussed at that meeting. However, I'm sure that this was not the focus of that meeting. Maybe only some sort of information was provided to General Sefer Halilovic to that effect. However, I cannot say anything about that because I can't remember that this topic was discussed at this meeting in any way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: So this would imply, for instance, that someone spoke to Halilovic, some international observer during breaks or informally, if I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. You have misunderstood me. I cannot confirm this. I don't know what was being discussed during the break, who was it who talked to General Sefer Halilovic. I cannot confirm that anybody from the international community had any sort of conversation during a break with General Sefer Halilovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: I wasn't implying that. I was only supposing that if he had some information, if he received some information on that day, it would not be -- have been during the official meeting. That is the point of my question. But you are saying in the official part of the meeting "I do not recall that the foreign fighters were mentioned."

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. You're right. I can't recall that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: We have no disagreement or no difference of opinion. I'm asking you this because the 20th of April is a few days after the kidnapping of Totic. And on the evening of the 21st, you are all discussing the problems of foreign fighters among each other with Halilovic being present. So if you told us that you presented the problem of the mujahedins to the general command staff, then -- well, let me say it in another way. Let me first go to the document that is the war diary. You have been presented with the original a few days ago. Let me not -- I don't think it's necessary to show you to the full extent. The commander of the 3rd Corps is opening the meeting by making a reference to the possible cease-fire. Then Halilovic is speaking. He is covering various topics. And then he says "the international dimension as regards the lack of control of the mujahedins and the like." I don't think it's in your binder, but if you would like to read it, we may produce it. May I ask the Registrar again to put P794 to the witness. If need be, I can give you the copy, although it is not quite proper. If you give me one copy of the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have got a spare copy that we can provide to the witness, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: The Defence in the case of Kubura, Mr. Ibrisimovic, offers to provide you with the text of the original.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've got it, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, if everybody's in agreement that we should follow this procedure, then I'll go on. On the first page of your copy, Witness, the B/C/S version, at the lower half of the page you see that Halilovic is taking the floor. Halilovic is speaking, and he says a number of things. And one of the things he said, I think it's better for me to read it in the English text, and you confirm whether you have found it. He says at a given moment: "The international dimension as regards the lack of control over the mujahedins and the like." This is my translation of the original Bosnian version text. Can you find the corresponding part in the original? I think it's the last line of the first page, and it continues on the second page.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have found part of the text where the word mujahedin is mentioned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: And would you please read it out for us in order to be able to check whether the translation is a proper one.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, I will read what it says here. "The international dimension of the failure to control the mujahedin and the like." End of quote.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: Thank you. That is about the same as the translation we have on paper. Now, there is no need for us to go through the whole minutes of the meeting. It's a rather long meeting, and please accept -- believe me if I'm saying that this is the only part of the record of the meeting where the problem is mentioned. I have not been able to find any other parts of the record of the same meeting discussing the same problem. So as a record of the meeting, it's very short compared to what you told us a few days before. And I understand, of course, that a war diary is not a newspaper. I also understand that a war diary is not a report or interim report, let alone a novel. They have to be short, these diaries. So it is possible that they do not reflect the real nature of the discussion. One thing I tend to believe, if reading this very short line, is the following: I get the impression that Halilovic was the one who began the discussion on the matter. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, what you have said and what has been presented to me by way of the minutes of this meeting would point to that. However, I know that within the system of command and control, the superior officer is informed about problems in the area of responsibility of a unit when he arrives in that area in somewhat greater detail than are mentioned in here. I believe that General Halilovic did have information, more detailed information before he uttered this word here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: And was the information coming from the -- from you or other members of the 3rd Corps, or did he have information already when he arrived in Zenica?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, we drafted reports. We sent those reports to our superior command. I can't recall the exact times and what these reports contained. I remember, however, that the information on the kidnapping of Zivko Totic arrived from the European Monitoring Mission. As far as I can remember, this was prior to the date when this meeting was held, i.e., prior to the 20th of April 1993 in which case, it would be obvious that the mujahedin represented a major problem and that more specific measures were to be taken against them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: If I understand you well, you are saying he may have had -- I mean Halilovic may have had reports from the 3rd Corps on the problem before coming to Zenica on the 21st. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, I cannot confirm this. I don't know whether he had information from the 3rd Corps prior to his arrival in Zenica. I never said that. I said that he might have had information. I don't know how he was informed about the problem of foreigners prior to his arrival in Zenica. I only know that we did have problems with foreigners. I have already testified to that effect before this Trial Chamber. But we did not consider this problem considerable for the 3rd Corps. It was only after the kidnapping of Zivko Totic did we believe that the 3rd Corps command should get involved in dealing with this problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: Well, in that case, I have indeed misunderstood your previous answer. It was not clear to me. And it's now clear that he had information from other sources.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have been presented with a document. I don't know whether this is a Prosecution exhibit or a Defence exhibit. It was the document of the Ministry of the Interior of Bosnia and Herzegovina which pointed to the problem of foreigners who had been arrested. However, before the kidnapping of Zivko Totic, this did not represent a problem for the 3rd Corps. And the 3rd Corps never thought that it should address this issue before the kidnapping of Zivko Totic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: Let me explain to you what I'm trying to establish. I'm trying to establish what was the knowledge of Halilovic at the time he came to Zenica, whether he got information from the 3rd Corps before he came or information from other sources. But as far as I understand you now is that you simply don't know. That's the final conclusion I would like to draw from what you said. Is that correct? Because it's not always easy to -- for you to know what I intend to say and for me to know what you intend to say.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is correct, Your Honour. I don't know because Sefer Halilovic never spoke to me about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: Thank you. I think we both deserve a break.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, we do indeed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We shall now adjourn, and we shall resume at 2.00. --- Luncheon recess taken at 12.32 p.m. 25 Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. The hearing is resumed. It is now 2.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness. Before the break, we have discussed Maline, and we were busy discussing the foreign fighters issue. I forgot to put you one question that I intended to put you on Maline. It is the final question I would like to put to you. It's the following: It struck me that the letter of Delic, the supreme command staff commander, was written on the 17th of October, and the request for information of the commander of the 3rd Corps also has the date 17th October. Now, this report that you received and on which you based your own report on the events dates from the 19th of October, and your report is dated the 21 of October. So there are four days between Delic's letter and your report. The question I have is you based your report on what you knew from your trip to Maline in August and also on the report of Asim Delic -- Rasim Delic. Did you consider additional steps of inquiry, or did you not?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I personally did not consider taking any other measures because the information which I had received indicated that these people were killed in combat. I've already explained this, Your Honours. It was not possible to investigate all killings which had occurred in the course of combat.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: I'm asking this because the --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: I'm asking this because the report of Rasim Delic's is rather short. It's a few lines, and that's it. That made me think whether you have considered additional steps of inquiry.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I think I've already answered that question. Namely, based on the reports I had at my disposal, there had been combat activity during which some people were killed. This is the information I would at the time. And based on that information, I produced my report, based on the information that I had in my possession about the events at the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: Let's go back to the foreign fighters issue then. We were discussing the meeting at which Halilovic was present, other meetings on the 21st of April. You also mentioned a second meeting which took place in May, another meeting in Zenica with Halilovic. And you said on the 9th of December here that at a meeting, it was suggested that two people from the supreme command should deal with the issues very seriously because the corps command was not capable of dealing with the issues on their own. Now, my question is, those two people from the supreme command who should deal with the issues very seriously, do you still remember their names?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember their names. Those were members of the supreme command staff, Mr. Rasim Delic and Mr. Sakib Mahmuljin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: And -- I'm sorry. And before the commander of the 3rd Corps, Hadzihasanovic, wrote his letter of June, his letter of the 13th of June, did you hear anything from the command?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I didn't understand the question. Do you mean from the superior command or subordinate command? You were not specific enough.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: I mean from the superior command, yes.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I did not have any other information at my disposal. It was not known to me whether any other information had arrived from the supreme command staff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: Now, let's turn to the letter of the 13th of June which is in your binder that the Defence gave you. Do you still have it with you? That's number 2 -- no, it's number 3 in the collection.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've found it, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: I have a few questions to put to you. Maybe you cannot answer them, but then let me know. I'll read you the first lines, the first linea. It says the following: "In the general area of Zenica Municipality since the beginning of the war, there have been volunteers from foreign countries, Arabs, Turks, as well as a group of Bosnians trained by them, the so-called guerrilla who have not entered the ranks of the BH Army in spite of being invited to." The next sentence is: "They are still contemplating the proposals made to them by the BiH Army chief of staff." Now, my question is the following: I note that they have been invited to enter the army and also that they are still contemplating the proposals made to them by the ABiH Army's chief of staff. This suggests that something has been done between the main meeting and this letter. I don't know what. Maybe you don't know what. But I'm wondering what has happened in the meantime?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I cannot remember what went on in between these dates that you have mentioned. However, I can repeat the general position that I've reiterated several times already; namely, that all of those who wanted to fight for freedom and independence of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina have to be under one single command. And if there are any groups outside of that system, they have to be placed under the command and follow the orders of the top leadership of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: You said before -- I don't quite recall on what day, but you said before regarding this letter that your commander may have had more knowledge than you. That may have been the case apparently if you don't know what this letter points to. Is that a fair conclusion, that you simply did not -- that you simply were not able to follow everything that developed?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm testifying here about what I know and what I saw. I'm also giving evidence about the information at my disposal. I cannot remember that I phrased it in exactly those terms; namely, that my commander, General Hadzihasanovic, had communication with someone regarding that, someone other than the supreme command staff. What I said was that there was communication with the supreme command staff. This is what I gave evidence, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: That's right. And that's also what I was saying. But the point of the question is you didn't know anything more than you told us before. Now, let's turn to the second linea --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could Your Honour please tell us the number of the exhibit you're reading from.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: You said the following: "They were in this territory even before the formation of the 3rd Corps." I'm sorry, this is DH165, number 1. The second linea of this text says the following: "They were in this territory even before the formation of the 3rd Corps, and fighting to date they have been acting outside the usual context and lawful methods of combat which is directly detrimental to the BH State and especially to the RBH Army." This reference to "outside the usual context and lawful methods of combat," this might be - this is my question to you - a reference to the events of Miletici on which you told us already a number of things. Is that correct? Or are you not able to say anything about it?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I really cannot entirely understand your question. This document which is under 3, number 3 in my package, is the one we focussed our attention on first and then we switched to document number 2, and then we are saying that those foreigners were present there even before the 3rd Corps was established. Your Honours, I simply cannot testify about that because I don't know whether these are the same people. In this text, under number 1, this text that you have just shown me, it is stated that these are representatives of humanitarian organisations, whereas the people who kidnapped Mr. Totic and who, let us assume the worst, also committed the murders in Miletici, then I really couldn't tell you whether these are the same people. You're asking me to confirm that these are the same people, but I cannot do that, Your Honours, because I don't know that. I don't know if I understood your question well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: I wonder if we have the same text. I'm discussing the letter of the 13th of June. Do you have that before you?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right, Your Honours. The document under number 3 is the one I have here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: You said that the letter mentioned representatives of humanitarian organisations. I don't see that in my translation. My translation runs "volunteers from foreign countries, Arabs and Turks" in the second line. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, yes, that's right. This is what is stated in my document. However, further into your question when you elaborated on the context, you stated that the foreigners were present there even before the 3rd Corps was established. And then you wanted me to focus on the document under number 1 in my package, which is dated February 1993. And this is what I do not understand because in February 1993, the establishment of the 3rd Corps had begun.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues]... conclude. I'm only talking about the document of the 13th of June, not another document.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour. I've understood now. We are now referring only to the document dated the 13th of June 1993, which is what I have in front of me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: I was reading to you the second linea of this document, of the 13th of June. It says "they were in this territory even before the formation of the 3rd Corps. In fighting to date, they have been acting outside the usual context of lawful methods of combat which is directly detrimental to the BH State and especially to the RBH Army." And I invited you to comment on that by asking you could this remark have something to do with the events in Miletici?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Your Honours. I interpret this somewhat differently. When they say "before the 3rd Corps was established," and I've already testified about this, Your Honours. In November of 1992 I heard rumours that in the defence of Karaula, several foreigners had been observed defending Karaula from the Serb aggressor who was very successful at the time. The situation was quite chaotic in the territory. At the time, only the Territorial Defence existed. The 3rd Corps was nowhere near being established. This is what I testified about, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: Now, that may be the case. But it is hardly perhaps a reason to write a letter to the supreme command in June. The second sentence of the second linea says "in fighting to date, they have been acting outside the usual context..." So that covers the whole period until the 13th of June, I would say. And in this context, I put this question: Could this have anything to do with Miletici?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Your Honours. I mentioned here another case of combat activity when in December the blockade of Sarajevo was being prepared, Sarajevo, the capital of Bosnia and Herzegovina. I gave evidence about the fact that already at the time I had some information about the engagement of a group of foreigners who had arrived in the territory, participated in combat activities, suffered losses, and then went back or went somewhere. We didn't establish where. They inflicted great damage at the time. Their behaviour was quite destructive. The members of the BH Army even captured some of them, and they were quite angry and wanted to kill the foreigners because somebody had blamed members of the BH Army for those terrible things that had been committed in the defence of the capital of Bosnia and Herzegovina. I've already testified about this, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: I know you testified already about that, but this letter is of the 13th of June, perhaps five months or more later than these events you are referring to. The text says "in fighting to date..." That means, in theory, linguistically, "until now," I would say.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct, Your Honours. I interpret it in the same way as you because November 1992 and December of 1992 were chronologically before the 13th of June 1993. Therefore, we think identically, Your Honours, you and I. This was the time when we received some rumours that there had been some foreigners, small groups of them, participating in combat activities. This text here mentions that, and they were involved in some combat activities. I don't know if this was clear enough, Your Honours. Perhaps you could reformulate your question so that I could be more specific. All of this took place before the 13th of June 1993. And as for Miletici, I don't know what specifically you're interested in, what context are you interested in? I stated that the BH Army was not involved in any combat activity in Miletici. When the events took place in Miletici, that was on the 24th of May -- no, I apologise. The 24th of April 1993. We had no combat activity in which members of the BH Army were involved at that time. This context that you read out cannot be linked in any way to the events in Miletici. Your Honours, I don't know if I succeeded in answering your question, but this is how I interpreted your question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: Let me make myself clear. I'm only asking you questions. I'm not venturing any opinion myself on how I should read, only to the extent that this seems to cover the whole period up to the 13th of June. Now, what strikes me is that on the 13th of June, your commander finds it necessary to write this letter. You already had two meetings with the supreme command staff, in April and in May. And your commander found it necessary to write a letter in June. Apparently he had very good reasons to do that at that moment. And I'm looking for an explanation. And I asked you, could it be that the events of Miletici prompted him to write this letter. That is the point of my question, and that is what I'm asking you.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, as far as is known to me, I believe that I could understand well the conduct of my commander, General Hadzihasanovic. Practically, this was the first written document sent to the supreme command staff. Everything that my commander, General Hadzihasanovic, informed the supreme command staff about was simply oral briefing during meetings, or there was perhaps some other means of communication as well. However, this here before us is an official, written document where my commander asks for a written reply about the problems encountered by us in the area of our responsibility.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: May I presume what you said so far by saying you're not able to tell us what prompted the letter of the 13th of June? Or do I misunderstand you now?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, you asked me about my opinion. I told you what my opinion about this matter was. I did not ask my commander to brief me on everything that he did, on every action of his. All I'm doing is now stating my opinion about this letter, which is what you've asked me to do.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're right, Your Honour. Now, as I'm testifying here and having the knowledge of all of the facts that I do, I really couldn't say that this document is related to the events in Maline. I really couldn't say that, Your Honour, because I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: All right. Neither do I know whether this played a role. That's why I'm asking you. And one of the reasons why I'm asking is this is that -- this letter is of the 13th of June, and the events in Maline were on the 8th of June. So if you have -- if there's a problem with foreign fighters, then this would be the moment to write a letter to the supreme command. That is a possible interpretation. I don't say it is the correct interpretation, but it is one of the interpretations you could have. This is by way of explaining why I'm asking this.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I should tell you with all the information that I have available to me now, that I'm testifying before this Court, the answer to that question, then I completely agree with you. But I have to go back to the time when this document was written. At that time, I was not able to draw that conclusion. I did not have that information on the 13th of June. But now when you set all the dates in chronological order and when I make the connections in my mind, it is certain that the 13th of June is really a date that follows the 8th of June.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: All right. I was only talking about a possible connection with Maline. I'm not suggesting that there is a connection, but only -- I'm only trying to verify whether -- what you know about the relationship. So your answer satisfies me in that respect. Now, let's turn to the text of the second linea. There's an additional sentence that I'll read now to you. It says the following: "It is a known fact that some state organs and higher-ranking Muslim clergymen are behind them." "It is a known fact..." Is that also something that you have knowledge about, that some state organs and high-ranking Muslim clergymen are behind them, or don't you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, I cannot remember having talked to the commander in that way. I don't remember discussing any assumptions about who could be standing behind those foreigners. I only recall that operative measures were taken by security services, among others, and I already explained what I mean by "operative measures." I am certain that one of the measures was to put the foreigners under surveillance, to wiretap the conversations, to try to infiltrate their man into that group. You know Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. that this job is highly, highly confidential, and any knowledge about it is limited to the very small circle of people implementing those operative measures. I am not familiar, Your Honour, with the exact operative measures taken by the security organs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: All right. Let's go further. We have this letter of the 13th of June. You were also shown the response by Commander Delic, which is of the 16th of June. It's the next document, that's DH165, number 2. You have explained the difficulties the 3rd Corps had with that response, "send them to Mount Igman," and this has been discussed in great length during the past days. Then there is another letter of Delic of the 23rd of July, this is DH165 number 4 authorising Sakib Mahmuljin to find a solution. Then in the next month, we come to a letter of the 12th of August, DH165, number 5, which is a proposal by the commander of the 3rd Corps to establish a unit, El Mujahid or El Mujahedin. And then there is a order, the final order of Delic, of the 13th of August, which is DH165, number 6. And this set of documents concludes by an order of the commander of the 3rd Corps with regard to the subordination of this unit to the 306th Brigade. Now, the whole time span is between the 13th of June when the commander of the 3rd Corps wrote his letter to the supreme command. And you have then the order of Delic of August the 13th settling the issue finally and saying "my order should be implemented before the end of the month August." I'm not going to discuss these documents with you, except for the order of Delic of the 13th of August. This is number 8 in your binder, I think. Let me check. Document DH165, number 6.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I've found the document here in my file under number 8. It's an order by the headquarters of the supreme command of the 13th of August 1993.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: That's the document I wanted to discuss with you. I only want to discuss with you the texts under II. It says "mobilisation preparations." Could you read out to us what is said below II.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can read it, Your Honour. And I will. "Reinforce detachment El mujahedin from the men, that is, foreign nationals - volunteers - who are located in the area of responsibility of the 3rd Corps. The said personnel is carrying weapons and other supplies that have been issued to them."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: This is slightly different from the translation we have in English. I'll read it before you, and maybe you could then comment on it. In the translation, it says the following: "These people keep their weapons and other equipment which has already been issued to them." I'm curious to know how this has been translated in B/C/S, but I'm unable to check. Is what you read something different from what has been translated from English into B/C/S?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I see the difference, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: What is the difference, according to you?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can recall the text that you read, which has officially been interpreted to me relative to the text I see in front of me, I see the difference in this part. "The weapons and other equipment they are to continue to carry." "The weapons and other equipment that had already been issued to them by somebody." I don't know by whom. That's the point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: The text as it has been translated in English that -- or as you read it in B/C/S on page 69, lines 5 and 6, says "the said personnel is carrying weapons and other supplies that have been issued to them." My question is really the following: If the commander says weapons and supplies that have been issued to them, I would be curious to know who issued these weapons and supplies and when? And my question is are you able to comment on that? Do you have any idea? Do you know? If you don't, say it. But that is my question.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, I could not clarify this. I'm not in a position to explain. I don't know who issued weapons to those people.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: Could you say- that is maybe not a good question to you - but if I read a sentence like this, I am inclined to think that those who will receive the order know what he is talking about. Would you like to comment on that, or wouldn't you?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Really, Your Honour, I could not give any comment because I have absolutely no knowledge about this. I could not really comment. I really don't know who gave them weapons, who issued weapons to them. I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: Now, yesterday, you told us about some combat operations in which the foreign fighters refused to fight, and that resulted in many casualties, and you also quoted the comment of the commander on that event. I heard you telling this -- I'm not quoting because I was not able to write down exactly what you said, but you did not mention any date or place, and I was afterwards looking for a document that would mention the same event as you spoke. Could you tell us what kind of event you were referring to, in what months of what year and what place?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, to the best of my recollection, it was in the beginning of September 1993. And to be even more precise, it was maybe the 5th or the 6th of September 1993 when they were resubordinated to the operational group Bosanska Krajina. Bosnian Krajina, and they were included, involved, in a combat activity in the area of Kruscica. The commander of the brigade which engaged part of its forces in that area, Fikret Cuskic, said later that part of the combat activities as a result of the behaviour of those foreigners resulted in great losses that this commander suffered in the broader area of Kruscica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: All right. Since I did not know what date and what place you were pointing to yesterday, I was looking for some documents in trying to find what you were talking about. I found another document that I may show you now. And it describes basically a similar situation, I would say. I would like you to comment on it. I'll ask you whether you recognise that situation. That document is of the 10th of August, and it has the number P477. I would like you to have a look at it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] While the document is being searched for, I would like to come back to the previous document regarding the interpretation or translation of this second paragraph. I would like to seek official translation of this second paragraph because when I compare now the Bosnian and the English text, I see that in English, it says that something had earlier been issued to those men, whereas in the Bosnian text, I see that it says that this concerns materiel that is currently in the possession of those men. This is perhaps not a great deal, but it is essentially different from the text of the translation we have now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: I agree with you. But this is the third translation of the same phrase. I think the translation in English that was given to us when the witness read the sentence is slightly different from what you said. Maybe we would have to ask again for an authorised translation. If we cannot be sure what is the translation, well, let's decide then if you all agree to have an authorised translation in the same manner we had some days ago.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is precisely why I am on my feet. I wanted to ask for an authorised translation of this second paragraph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mr. Registrar, the Chamber is requesting an authorised translation of Document P477. The translation would be submitted to us when we come back in January.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: In the meantime, Witness, do you have this document, P477, of the 10th of August 1993?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have in front of me a document dated the 9th of August 1993.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: Now, as you see, this is a report to the supreme command staff by the commander of the 3rd Corps, and it is of -- on the various operations groups in his command. First, there is the operations group Bosna. And then under 3, you have the operations group Zapad. And under 4, you have Lasva. This is quite a long text. But have a look at the paragraph under 1.2, "our forces." In my English translation, this would be line 8, and it starts with the following words: "The Muslim forces or mujahedin brought from Travnik as well as the part of Muslim forces from Zavidovici..." Do you find this line? Are you able to spot where I am now?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I noticed -- I located this passage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: Could you read for us, sir, what is said in this sentence and the following sentences.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters' request: Could it be put on the ELMO, please, because we don't have this document. In the original, if possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: The B/C/S text, of course, not the English text.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm taking advantage of this situation to make a correction. I'm not asking for -- we are not asking for the authorised translation of P477, but of DH165.6. You have the document P477 in your language, Witness?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I have the document in front of me in the Bosnian language.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: It's not on the ELMO as the interpreters requested, but maybe... Now, could you read to us the lines I indicated and that you have been able to find now.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The passage that you indicated, Your Honour, I found it. And I can read it out. I can read a sentence out of that passage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: I would like to ask you, this is quite a job for you to read the whole until the end of the 1.2. It's a long text, I know. But then everybody's able to hear what the text is.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I read the entire passage up to subitem 1.2, then it becomes completely unclear to me because you read a part of the text from item 1.2. And now you want me to read up to 1.2. Did I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: I think there is again a misunderstanding. We started by saying there is -- I started by saying there is a paragraph 1.2, "our forces." And then I said at line 8 or 9, there is a sentence beginning with the words, "the Muslim forces or mujahedin brought from Travnik," and I asked you did you find it? And you said yes. And now I'm asking you to start reading from that point, not from 1.1, but 1.2, the part where this sentence begins. Is that clear now?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the Bosnian language here, I have item 1.2. I've found this passage. And it goes to item 2, up to the subheading OG Istok, OG East. Is that the passage you mean?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: Yes, I said already that's quite a length. But could you nevertheless read it for the benefit of all of us. Some of us don't have this document.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The planned offensive" -- sorry, sorry. I should start earlier. "Muslim forces," is that where you want me to start?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: That's where I want you to start, yes.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Muslim forces or mujahedin brought from Travnik as well as the part of Muslim forces from Zavidovici did not want to carry out the order. Those forces, together with the part of the 314th Motorised Brigade, were supposed to attack along the axis Petrovici" -- the following word is not quite legible. Then goes Misici, trig point 323. "Thorough reconnaissance has been carried out with the aforementioned, and not for a second had they shown a single sign that they would refuse to carry out the assigned task. Readiness for execution of the task was 2100 hours on the 8th of August 1993 for all units. At 1900 hours, they reported that they could not carry out combat activities by night, and I postponed readiness for all units to 500 hours on the 9th of August 1993. "At 0400 hours, they refused the order again, stating as a reason that they do not trust the army and fear treason. In view of the planning and the fact that the execution of the task by the 314th Motorised Brigade and 318th Motorised Brigade depended on it, I gave the order to cease the action until further notice. Due to the conduct of this group of mujahedin from Travnik, so far one can assume that they had been dispatched to me or sent to me for the purpose of spreading some culture unknown to me. In the course of the day, they shall be returned to where they have come from. The rest of the Muslim forces from Zavidovici Municipal Staff I will most probably disband and distribute them among the battalions of the 318th Mountain Brigade."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: Thank you. There is another part in the same document which deals with the operations group Lasva, and it more or less tells the same story, but I will not ask you to read it. This part of the report that you have read before us reminds me a little bit of what you told about the problems in September in the units of Fikret Cuskic. Do you agree that you recognise a pattern of these persons not being prepared to perform what they had promised to do? Or what they were supposed to do?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, I see a great difference here between what we had on the 6th of September 1993 and what we have here dated the 9th of August 1993.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: There is no mention of casualties as a consequence of their behaviour. That is obvious. But I pointed out the fact that they, so to speak, went their own way, made their own decisions, that for me is a similarity. Maybe I am mistaken. Please tell me.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, as I interpret this text that I've read out, and taking into account what we've already said about the document dated September of 1993, this document dated the 9th of August 1993 clearly indicates that the mujahedin had been brought there, or the Muslim forces, the mujahedin. The author of this document cannot define them because the author says the Muslim forces or the mujahedin. Therefore, he doesn't know the difference between the Muslim forces and the mujahedin. And the document from September of 1993 very clearly spells out and orders the mujahedin detachment, which had been established somewhat earlier to be resubordinated to the Bosanska Krajina operative group. In military terms, Your Honour, the difference is huge. It is so significant that these two things cannot be compared even. I've mentioned several times that in the BH Army, there were not Muslim forces, and there were no mujahedin up until the mujahedin detachment was established. I state that with full responsibility. Therefore, these Muslim forces or the mujahedin as they are referred to in this text had been brought in from Travnik by someone. Now, in military terms, who can bring in someone and who cannot is quite a significant matter. There are very strict rules about who can issue orders or who can send somebody in military terms. Nobody can bring in a unit, especially not a unit that is not familiar to anyone. This text here refers to the Muslim forces or mujahedin. Therefore, the person who wrote this document did not know who these people were and who had brought them in. For me, Your Honours, this is a tremendous difference for me as a military person.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: I agree with you that the text of September is an order, and this is not an order. This is a combat report. It's not -- that is something different. If you point at that, that is quite proper to do so. But I also draw your attention to the very end of the document. It is purported to be a document written by the commander of the 3rd Corps, Enver Hadzihasanovic, although I do not see a signature. But this may be due to the fact that it has been communicated to the supreme command, and apparently this document in the form we have it comes from the archives of the supreme command. But it bears the name at the end of the commander Enver Hadzihasanovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have the original?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, we will make the efforts to do that. It may take us a little bit of time. Perhaps by the time we recommence after the next break we'll have it, but Mr. Vatter will do what he can do get us that as quickly as possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: Well, I guess it will not be an enhanced signature, because it was communicated by electronic means, and that means very often that the signature gets lost. But let's not dwell on it any further. I would like to show you another document. That is Document P434 of the 12th of July.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, with your leave, I would like to make a comment. You first put a question to me, and then you interrupted me. I believe that I should answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: Well, I'm not aware of having you interrupted. At any rate, that is not intentional. But if I did so, please tell me what you intended to tell.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I don't know what is stated in your English version, but as was interpreted to me into my native language through my headphones, I understood you to inquire as to whether this document was created by Commander Hadzihasanovic. I can assure you with full responsibility that my commander, General Hadzihasanovic, would never have authored a document of this nature.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: I take note of that. Let's have a look at Document P434. And for the benefit of the parties, I may mention that there are two other documents related to the same events or the same day, same -- well, event is maybe the best word. That is P603 and P604. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. You have this document before you, General? 12th July 1993.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Dated 12th of July, yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: Let's look first to the signature. It says "Commander Enver Hadzihasanovic," but it's not his signature, I suppose, as far as I'm able to tell. Could you confirm that.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, I can read what is stated here. "Commander Hadzihasanovic," however, the word Enver is hidden by the seal. I can see only the letter R. I can see the signature clearly. And you're absolutely right, Your Honour. This is not General Hadzihasanovic's signature.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: My question is whose signature is it? Could you recognise the signature?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, I cannot recognise the signature. It is not familiar to me. I am very well familiar with the signature of General Hadzihasanovic. It is quite a unique signature and can be deciphered very easily. I don't know who signed this, though.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: So would you please read what is stated in this document, this -- which is called query.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean this text?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: Read it to yourself to start with to get familiar with the content.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've read it, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: Maybe I could also give you Document P603. I think it's better to show you also this document. It is two days earlier. It is the 10th of July. And here again, if you look at the end, it mentions the name of the commander of the 3rd Corps, but the signature is different. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've read it, Your Honour. I've read this document as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: Now, the second document that you read -- that you received in a minute before is a letter to the 333rd Mountain Brigade. And the first document, which is two days later, is a document that is addressed to the 7th Mountain Brigade. Let me explain what I -- what my understanding of the two documents is, and then you may comment on whether I read this properly or not. I understand that the 333rd Mountain Brigade is in some difficulty and needs military assistance. And I also understand that it has asked help from the commander of the 3rd Corps. This is clearly stated in Document 604, but for the sake of time I have not shown you that. Now, in the second document of the 10th of July, it is said that "since the mentioned unit is not part of the BH Army, we cannot issue orders to it." And secondly "we approve the use of this unit as previously agreed." And third: "In the event of this unit's engagement, inform this command in a combat report." And the second document of the 12th of July is addressed to those who should be -- who should offer assistance to the 333rd Mountain Brigade. It's a call for help of the 7th Mountain Brigade -- 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade, and it is conditional on something. That is apparent in the first part of the text. It says "since the engagement of Arabs who are ready to carry out combat activities in the 333rd Brigade zone of responsibility, it is conditional on joint combat together with your unit." And therefore, to summarise what is said, let me know if you are -- whether you are prepared to offer assistance, the implication being that if you are ready to offer assistance, those Arabs who are already carrying out combat activities will also join the fight. That is my understanding of these two documents. I don't know whether you are of the same or of a different opinion.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, you are giving us your thoughts regarding these documents. I personally partially disagree with you because I have a different opinion and a different interpretation of these documents. Your Honour, I will simply point out to those parts where I disagree with you, which is the essence of what I'm trying to tell you. Therefore, you're asking me here for my opinion about these documents, and Your Honour, I will give you my opinion. Now as to whether my opinion will be the correct one, I don't know. I'm simply stating my opinion, and my perception of these documents. And if I understood you right, you're interested in my opinion about these documents. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: Yes, go ahead. That's what I'm asking you.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I naturally will not read out everything. I will simply mention the details which in my view are essential. The document dated the 10th of July, under item 2, it is stated that this is being approved "in accordance with previous agreement." I, as a soldier, think that it should be stated here "in accordance with previous orders" because there are no agreements in the army, only orders. I don't know who, whether the person who authored this document or the persons who prepared these documents had some previous agreements and arrangements. This obviously has to do with the assistance to the 333rd Brigade. Therefore, I believe you when you say that you found the document indicating that the 333rd Brigade was facing some difficulties. However, I, as a soldier, believe that within the command and control system, there are no agreements and arrangements. Soldiers cannot say "we will do this now, but on the next occasion maybe we won't do it." There are only orders. In the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, in the command and control system, only orders are recognised. Therefore, the text should say "in accordance with previous orders," not "in accordance with previous arrangements or agreements." I cannot accept this formulation. If we look at these documents, and this is the first time that I see these documents - I had no opportunity to see them earlier - I see that mention is made of Arabs, as you have stated yourself. However, based on this document, it is not clear to me that they were an integral part of the 7th Muslim Brigade because the text here indicates that they are ready to carry out combat activities together with your unit. Therefore, if these Arabs are within the 7th Muslim Brigade, then they cannot give any conditions because they are an integral part of this brigade. And in that case, they can't say in this text "together with your unit." Therefore, on the basis of this text, I can only conclude that the Arabs were absolutely not an integral part of the 7th Muslim Brigade. Further on, as I read this text, there's a request here to place reserve forces, the 3rd Company of the 3rd Battalion of the 7th Muslim Brigade, and this is something that I can accept; namely, that this company ought to be ready, waiting in reserve to assist the 333rd Brigade. Your Honour, I disagree with you on the score that there can be some agreements in the army, that people can agree or disagree on something. In my view, the Arabs mentioned here were not within the 7th Muslim Brigade because had there been an integral part of the intrigued, the text formulation would have been different. No doubt about it. Your Honours, this is what I keep reiterating, that these forces which are mentioned here and there in smaller or greater numbers, better or worse equipped, were not within the corps, the 3rd Corps. And when measures were made at the highest level to place those forces under the command of the 3rd Corps, they refused to carry out orders in the approved system, in the established system, within the command and control system. And I spoke quite a lot about that, Your Honour. Therefore, to conclude, there can be no arrangements or agreements made within the Army, and I interpret these documents to mean that Arabs were not an integral part of any formation of any brigade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: Well, that's exactly the point I am trying to make. I'm not saying -- I have never said that these people were members of the 7th Brigade or any other brigade. I'm just asking you, and this is my reading of the document, that outside the army, there were groups as mentioned in the previous document of August that I've shown to you, and now in these two documents. There are groups outside the army with which there is some form of cooperation. I would not know how to call it. Maybe horizontal cooperation, but nevertheless there is some cooperation. How unhappily commanders may be and disappointed by the results. But that is what I tend to read in the document, a form of cooperation, not with people who are in the army but with people who are outside the army. Let's continue after the break. We'll resume our discussions on these documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is now 3.30. The hearing will resume at 5 to 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The hearing is resumed. During the break, did you manage to find the original of the document?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Yes, we did, Mr. President. I'll pass this now to the usher. I did show it to counsel for the Defence during the break, but the accused obviously weren't present at that point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: Witness, we have the original document of the 9th of August, which is Number P477. Maybe it's good to show it to you because you had some comments on it.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, even last time I did not doubt the photocopy. I don't have any doubts about the papers that I'm being shown here. I only gave my comments in response to your question. Not for a moment did I doubt what you presented me with. I did not even ask to see the original.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: Nevertheless, we had a discussion, a short discussion, on the absence of a signature. I remember that was the one point we were discussing to some extent. Now, you see, as I see, that this is apparently a fax that has been sent by electronic means from one place to another. And usually, in such a situation, the original signature disappears, especially if you take into account the technique in 1993. If you fax a letter now, if I would fax you a letter and sign it, you would get my signature. But with the techniques available in 1993, I believe this was not yet possible. So in order to verify what kind of document it was, it is good to have a look at it. Now we are all able to see it is a fax, and that is the purpose of getting the original documents. And if I may add, it is always better to have an original document you can read it better, as you have seen this morning. There are more characteristics on an original that get lost in photocopies. But unfortunately, we all work mostly with copies, which is a huge disadvantage in a criminal trial. So that is the -- let me explain the reason why my colleagues and me thought it useful to have the original copy.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I understand, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mrs. Usher, please get the document back and return it to its owner.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: Now, to resume our discussion we had on the documents in July and August, as an outsider, I say with some emphasis, as an outsider, as someone who has not been in the army and certainly not in the army in Bosnia at the time as you were, when you read these documents on -- of August, the first document that you have seen, the document that you have looked at seconds ago, and when you look at the other documents that we have discussed before the break of July, as an outsider, I would say I get the impression, I must be very careful in expressing myself. But I get the impression - and this I want to check with you, and that is the purpose also of the whole exercise - that there was some sort of, let me say, horizontal cooperation of the army with group outside the army. I never say, and I repeat it again, these people were a member of the army. I have no opinion on that. But on the face of the documents, at first blush, you would say, there might be some form of horizontal cooperation, of people outside the army who under their own conditions from time to time participate in combat or do not participate after having promised to do so which causes enormous -- a lot of problems. But what I would like to have your opinion about is whether we are or I am right in reading this -- drawing these kind of conclusions from these documents. If you say "no," go ahead. You already have said no, and we'll take your opinion and your remarks into account, of course. It is important for us to know what you think about these documents. So that is -- that may explain why I am giving you these documents. And if you want to comment again upon these documents, please do.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have spoken extensively about these documents already as a professional man, although I can't say I'm a great expert. There are many better experts than I in specific fields. But as somebody who spent his life serving in the army, I commented upon this as a soldier in a particular line of service, and I said what I said. I can only repeat myself now. This horizontal link that you refer to sounds very interesting to me. It now affects my process of thinking, and maybe I could say something about that. As a soldier, I never see that horizontal link. You know how I view things as a soldier. There's always a vertical connection. You can have somebody by your side, but even in that horizontal connection everything has to be agreed, everything has to be specified. And if you conclude that there is a horizontal link, I will certainly not object to that conclusion. But in principle, I don't agree with that because there are no horizontal links in the army in terms of command and control. In that sense, the army is very precise. A horizontal link may exist with certain organisations with which certain arrangements are made. But in principle, there are no arrangements in the army. Orders are given, and they get executed or not executed. So that horizontal connection practically doesn't exist. It is alien to me. That's why I can't really comment upon horizontal links. There are professional connections in the army, links based on expertise. And if you talk about connection based on expertise which does exist in the global system of command, then in this case I don't see even that connection. There may be a connection between BH Army units and some groups which, as we see from this, are causing problems and somebody's making arrangements with them. I would really not be able to agree that this is a case of horizontal connection, speaking of the army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: I think we agree on the fact that horizontal relations in the army are not conceivable, so to speak, that the whole system of an army supposes vertical relationships. There's one at the top who gives command to the others who have to comply. And the whole concept of horizontal cooperation is utterly alien to the structure of an army, of a regular army. That, we agree upon. But I try to find an expression, a word for what I may have seen in these documents. Let me be very careful in expressing my thoughts. You understand what my problem is. Well, these are two documents that are in July -- of July 1993 and August 1993. This is in the period between the letter of 13 June of the commander of the 3rd Corps and the final order of Delic settling the issue by ordering the creation of a separate independent unit, El Mujahid or El Mujahedin. In your testimony of this afternoon, and even before, you refer to events in 1992. You refer to Karaula, battle for Karaula, and also to Visoko. Visoko I think was at the end of December 1992, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, as far as I'm able to recall, it was December.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: All right. And as far as Karaula is concerned, I don't know what month or what date -- or it may have been a very long period. Could you situate the time when there was a battle over Karaula.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, I said that it happened in November, roughly speaking. I can only give a precise chronology of events. I said we had problems defending Karaula when the aggressor captured Jajce. And a great number of people, both civilians and TO units that had been completely crushed, were engulfed in chaos. Lots of troops with no commander in sight. Everybody was mixed, people, cattle, livestock. I believe it would be hard for you to even imagine that sight. Shooting, all that mixed citizenry, Croats, Bosniaks, including people who had been expelled from their homes even earlier in Krajina. Bosniaks and Croats joined by people from Jajce, and then on top of that comes Karaula, aggravating the situation. I can only tell you that I got a lot of grey hair in those days. I was the one in charge, and I had to deal with it. It was really hard for me, and it took me a long time to recover from the shock. I can only place events in time. I think this was in November.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: You have mentioned the fall of Jajce, and quite a few other witnesses have also mentioned that crucial event in the autumn of 1992. As far as I can recall, no one has given us a specific date. Could you give me a date for the fall of Jajce.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, I cannot recall exactly the date. It was not a particular day that Jajce fell into the hands of the aggressor. That happened gradually. But from my point of view as a soldier, it happened rather quickly. We had forces defending Jajce. And without my notes, I would be hard put to give you a date. However, it happened over two or three days, maybe even five or six days. In any case, I can't recall the exact date.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: So we'll stick to the autumn of 1992. Because I'm unable to make it more specific at this moment. Now, what you said to us is that in Karaula and Visoko later on, a number of foreigners took part in battles. Maybe on their own initiative, without consulting any army unit, I don't know, but they were seen. And you confirmed the fact that foreigners had fought in these two events. And that's the only thing I know about that, and I know that, that you already said -- also said and other witnesses have said before about these two battles. Now, I have shown you a few documents from the period of July and August 1993 when a discussion was going on on what to do with these foreigners starting with the meeting in April, 21st of April. Then you Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. have this letter of the commander of the 3rd Corps to the supreme command staff saying "make clear what you want. There's a problem." And ending with the order of Delic of August, mid-August 1993. What happened in August -- or in July doesn't necessarily indicate what happened before. Apparently there is an evolving situation. We have in the beginning in 1992 two examples of foreigners taking part in battle under conditions that we know nothing about. We have the mujahedin unit as of the beginning of September, or maybe the last week of August. That is not important for me. And we have this period of discussions on the whole problem of foreign fighters within the army itself. There are still some months, the beginning of January to the letter of Hadzihasanovic saying "solve this problem. There is an urgent problem." Could you tell me what was the case, the situation during these months? And I would also like to discuss the situation of these months with you on the basis of, let's say, at least one document.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would like to make a remark. I heard interpretation into my language to the effect that in this period you refer to, up to August, they were in the ranks of the BH Army. I would appreciate it very much, and I don't know how you put it in English, but I already said yesterday that I had a lot of problems with interpretation. A lot of the time, I hear something different. And when everything has been read to me, I said that within a certain period, they were within the ranks of the BH Army. However, I would like the interpreter to be more careful, really.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: I agree with you that what you said now is not what I said to you. I did not state that they were in the ranks of the army up to August 1993. On the contrary. I said there was an intermediate stage in which discussions were taking part. They became a member of the army officially when the order of Rasim Delic took effect, and not before. So if you have understood that I said that before August they were part of the army, then this must be an error of translation. I did not want to say it, even if you may have heard it, I believe I did not say it. I am interested in the first months, the first six months, so to speak, before the whole discussion on what to do with the problem of foreign fighters in your area of responsibility became really acute. And I would limit myself to showing you one document and have your comments on that document in order to be able to assess the document better. And this is a document from the 19th of January 1993. And it has the Exhibit Number P702.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters' request: We do not have this document. If there will be any reading of it, then maybe it should be put on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: If you look at the bottom of the document in your version, you see the name of Selmo Cikotic. There is no signature. I don't know why. Maybe this again is a fax. I don't know. Maybe there are other reasons. Maybe it's not a document of Selmo Cikotic. And if you look at the top of the document, you see that it is -- this document is addressing -- is addressed to the 3rd Corps in Zenica, among other things. Now, I would like you to read the third paragraph of this document.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Requests: 1, that Lendo provide a man who would get to the village of Bistrica during the night and take over command over" - I suppose this means infantry company, the two initial letters are not quite clear to me - "from Novi Travnik. The mujahedin and the troops or forces from Bistrica. And then with these men, to execute an attack along the axis checkpoint in Bistrica village, Franjkovac Kupa, Zvizde, Gornji Vakuf, link up with the forces in town, and supply us with the materiel and technical equipment that is located there; two, provide supply of all types of assistance and provisions from the direction of Konjic towards Voljevac village; three, to have Lendo meet our request and open artillery fire at the designated targets; four, that the PDO anti-airborne assault defence commanded by Faruk Aganovic, Jupi, urgently be sent from Bugojno with a task to break through to Gornji Vakuf. He knows which direction to take; five, that the infantry weaponry be sent to the fighters of 305th Mountain Brigade."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: Thank you. What I want to discuss with you is the first sentence beginning with the words "that Lendo." You see the word "mujahedin" in his requests. And I would like to ask you -- I suppose you have never seen this document before. Could you answer that?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I'm seeing this document for the first time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
